newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.

text.p: The South African rand and key long bonds drifted steadily towards the close after giving up earlier Tuesday gains.
Bond traders reported some institutional profit-taking and said they expected the benchmark R150 bond to attract yields in a 15.10-15.20 percent range on Wednesday.
"We've got an options close-out on Thursday and that's going to determine our trading," one trader said.
Currency dealers said they had had a quiet day with a fair amount of import demand met by exporter interest.
"Not much really happened. There was just good two-way trade. It's too early to say what's likely to happen tomorrow. We will have to see what New York does tonight," one trader said.
The rand ended at 4.5270/5300 on the dollar compared to its 4.5335/5365 finish on Monday.
On the crosses, the rand eased against sterling to 7.3311/3405 versus 7.3039/3137 and was little changed on the mark at 0.3623/3626 compared to 0.3630/3633.
On the bond market, the key R150 bond was at 15.15 percent at 1430 GMT from 15.14 percent at the same time on Monday.
"We see it in a range of 15.10 to 15.20 percent tomorrow but that depends. We've got an options close-out on Thursday and that's going to determine our trade," one trader said.
"Maybe it will reach a strike level of 15.25 or the figure (15.00) or will be slap bang in the middle," he added.
Foreigners bought 60.16 million rands worth of South African bonds on Monday after buying 308.39 million rands worth on Friday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative turnover on the bond market on Monday was 7.03 billion from Friday's was 8.93 billion rand.

A rise in the money market shortage to 9.258 billion rand on Monday from 8.238 billion rand on Saturday was put down to the Reserve Bank drained liquidity after what dealers said were overdone falls last week.
Three-month NCDs were quoted slightly higher by South Africa's four major banks at 16.60 offered from 16.55-16.60 percent on Monday.
The 90-day BA rate was unchanged at between 15.95 percent and 16.15 percent bid.

The week's main economic indicator will be January reserves, due on Friday, with economists predicting a rise in gold and foreign exchange reserves to a six-month high of 11.2 billion rand from 10.3 billion in December.
January new car sales and the latest business confidence index are due on Wednesday.
